sentences.text: This extinct group included four valid species of large penguins.
Smaller members were roughly the size of an emperor penguin, while the biggest stood nearly 1.5 meters tall.
The species Palaeeudyptes antarcticus serves as the type species for the genus.
The largest species, Palaeeudyptes klekowskii, could reach two meters in length and weigh up to 116 kilograms.
Thomas Henry Huxley first described the genus in 1859.
A humerus bone identified as belonging to this genus was found in middle to late Eocene layers near Puerto Natales in southernmost Chile.
Its skeletal features were somewhat less advanced than those of Archaeospheniscus and roughly comparable to the gigantic Anthropornis.
The genus Palaeeudyptes provides the name for the subfamily Palaeeudyptinae.
The genus Eosphaeniscus, which Wiman described in 1905, is now considered a synonym of Palaeeudyptes.
Scientists do not yet know the exact evolutionary relationship between the subfamily Palaeeudyptinae and modern penguins.
The genus existed from the Lutetian to the Burdigalian stages, spanning between 48.07 and 15.98 million years ago.
